post.summary: Join or create an Abriyah shared room
post.description:
Match the calling rider into an Abriyah shared-ride room for their zone, opening a new room if none is available.

**Features:**
- Detects the Abriyah-enabled zone from the dropoff point (PostGIS containment); the pickup may be in any active service zone, so cross-zone trips into the dropoff zone are supported.
- Computes the per-rider fare from the PICKUP zone (its Abriyah params when Abriyah-enabled, falling back to the settings regular fare otherwise).
- Computes a per-rider fare as base + round(haversine_km * per_km), in integer IQD; coordinates are WGS84 lng/lat.
- Finds an open room of the requested type in the zone, or creates one with the zone's max-riders and max-wait-seconds expiry.
- Creates a matched Abriyah trip for the rider and links it to the new room member.
- Publishes room.opened/room.joined and trip.requested realtime events.

**Behavior:**
- Validates `room_type` is 'mixed' or 'women_only'.
- Women-only requests require a female rider (gender 'f') and a zone that allows women-only rooms.
- On the 201 the room may already be 'dispatched' if it filled while a captain was assigned; a full but captain-less room stays open.

**Restrictions:**
- Rider JWT required; the rider's gender is read from their user record.
- One active room per rider; joining again while already in a room is rejected.
- Returns 400 when the dropoff is not in an Abriyah-enabled zone, the pickup is outside any active service zone, women-only is not allowed in the dropoff zone, or `room_type` is invalid.

201.description: Rider matched into a room; returns the room, the new member, and the matched trip

400.description: Dropoff not in an Abriyah-enabled zone, pickup not in any active service zone, women-only not allowed in the dropoff zone, or invalid room_type

403.description: JWT role is not 'rider' (role-gated route), or a women-only room is requested by a non-female rider

409.description: Rider is already in an active room

delete.summary: Leave the rider's active Abriyah room
delete.description:
Remove the calling rider from their current Abriyah room and cancel their matched trip.

**Behavior:**
- Looks up the rider's active room and member; cancels the linked trip (system actor for matched, admin actor for accepted) with reason 'changed_mind'.
- Removes the member from the room and decrements the room's rider count.
- Publishes a trip.cancelled realtime event.
- Leaving after a captain has locked the room is allowed but logged as a warning.

**Restrictions:**
- Rider JWT required.
- Returns 400 when the rider is not in any active room.

200.description: Rider left the room and the trip was cancelled

400.description: Rider is not in any active room

get.summary: Get an Abriyah room with its members
get.description:
Retrieve a single Abriyah room and the list of riders currently seated in it.

**Returns:**
- The room (zone, type 'mixed'|'women_only', status 'open'|'locked'|'dispatched'|'expired', max/current rider count, assigned captain, expiry and timestamps).
- The room members, each with their per-rider fare (integer IQD), distance, and linked trip id. Member pickup/dropoff geometry is not included here.

**Use Cases:**
- The Customer App polling a room the rider has joined for fill progress and dispatch state.

**Restrictions:**
- Rider JWT required; no ownership check is performed (any authenticated rider may read any room by id).

200.description: The room and its current members

404.description: No room exists with this id

post.summary: Accept and dispatch an Abriyah room (captain)
post.description:
Assign the calling captain to an open Abriyah room, lock it, and immediately dispatch it to all seated riders.

**Behavior:**
- Verifies the captain is approved and not already on another active room.
- Requires the room to be in 'open' status; locks it to the captain (publishes room.locked).
- Dispatches the room: transitions it to 'dispatched' and advances every member trip from matched to accepted with this captain (optimistic-locked; concurrent transitions are skipped).
- Triggers a best-effort reports rollup and enqueues a push notification to each rider.
- Returns the resulting dispatched room.

**Use Cases:**
- A captain taking the next available Abriyah pool in their zone.

**Restrictions:**
- Captain JWT required; the captain must have status 'approved'.
- Women-only rooms require a female captain (gender 'f').
- Returns 400 if the room is not 'open', 403 if the captain is not approved or fails the women-only gate, 409 if the captain already has an active room.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Room ID (UUID) of the open room to accept

200.description: The room after it was locked and dispatched to the captain

400.description: Room is not in 'open' status

403.description: Captain not approved, or a non-female captain accepting a women-only room

404.description: No room exists with this id

409.description: Captain already has an active room assignment

get.summary: List a room's rider details (assigned captain)
get.description:
Retrieve the full per-rider detail for a room the calling captain is assigned to.

**Returns:**
- The `room_id`, the shared `dropoff_zone` (id + names), a `pickup_breakdown` (rider counts per pickup zone; a null-zone entry groups out-of-zone pickups), and the `members` roster (name, phone, pickup/dropoff WKT, per-rider fare, distance, join time).

**Use Cases:**
- The Captain App showing the pickup sequence and rider contacts for an in-progress Abriyah pool.

**Restrictions:**
- Captain JWT required; only the captain assigned to the room may read it.
- Returns 403 when the caller is not the assigned captain, 404 when the room id does not exist.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Room ID (UUID) the captain is assigned to

403.description: Caller is not the captain assigned to this room

404.description: No room exists with this id

post.summary: Validate Abriyah pickup and dropoff pins
post.description:
Check the pickup and dropoff pins for live feedback as the rider drags the map.

**Features:**
- Validates the two ends independently: the dropoff must fall inside an Abriyah-enabled zone AND the pickup inside any active zone (cross-zone Abriyah trips supported).
- Returns `valid`, the resolved `dropoff_zone_id`, the resolved `pickup_zone_id`, and a human-readable `message` for inline display in the Customer App. The request `zone_id` field is deprecated and ignored.

**Behavior:**
- This endpoint never returns an HTTP error for out-of-zone pins; invalid pins yield 200 with `valid:false` and an explanatory message.

**Access:**
- Public: no authentication required. It reads no rider data and mutates nothing (a stateless PostGIS check), mirroring `/api/trips/estimate` so the Customer App can validate pins as the rider drags the map before login.

200.description: Validation result with valid flag, resolved dropoff_zone_id and pickup_zone_id, and message

400.description: Malformed request body

get.description:
Retrieve the Admin Daily Activation Log: one row per captain per Asia/Baghdad calendar day, with a paginated, filtered list and a fee-sum footer.

**Features:**
- Filter by `date_from` / `date_to` (inclusive calendar-day bounds, Asia/Baghdad), `status` (pending | paid | waived), and `captain_id`.
- Offset pagination via `page` (1-based, min 1) and `page_size` (default 50, clamped to 1..=200).
- Each row joins the captain's name and phone plus the waiving admin's name (when waived).
- The body footer carries `total_fee_iqd` (sum of fees in integer IQD across the filtered set), `total` (matching-row count), `page`, and `page_size`.

**Use Cases:**
- Daily reconciliation of captain activation fees by an operator or finance admin.
- Drilling into a single captain's activation history via the `captain_id` filter.

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description:
Inclusive lower bound on the activation `date` (Asia/Baghdad calendar
day, YYYY-MM-DD). Null means no lower bound.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description:
Inclusive upper bound on the activation `date` (Asia/Baghdad calendar
day, YYYY-MM-DD). Null means no upper bound.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by activation state: "pending" | "paid" | "waived" | "failed".
Null returns all states.

parameters.name: captain_id
parameters.description: Filter to a single captain's activations. Null returns all captains.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number to return. Null defaults to the first page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of rows per page. Null applies the server default page size.

200.description: Paginated activation log rows with a fee-sum footer

get.description:
Fetch a single captain daily-activation record by its ID for the admin detail view.

**Returns:**
- The full `CaptainDailyActivation`: captain ID, the Asia/Baghdad calendar `date`, `fee_amount_iqd` (integer IQD), and `status` (pending | paid | waived).
- `collected_at` is set when `status` = paid (the captain wallet charge succeeded and stamped the collection time) and is null otherwise; `waived_by` and `waived_reason` are populated only when `status` = waived; `charge_error` carries the failure message only when a charge failed.

**Use Cases:**
- Inspecting one captain's activation status before deciding to waive the fee.
- Resolving a row opened from the Daily Activation Log.

404.description: No activation record with this ID

post.description:
Waive a captain's daily activation fee. Restricted to the super-admin role and requires an audited reason.

**Behavior:**
1. Trims the `reason` and rejects it when shorter than 10 characters (400).
2. Loads the activation record by ID; returns 404 when it does not exist.
3. Guards the current status: only a `pending` record can be waived. A record that is already `waived` or `paid` is rejected by the service guard (409); a `failed` record (its charge was rejected) passes the service guard but then loses the optimistic lock on the `WHERE status = 'pending'` update, so it also returns 409. In short, any non-pending status yields 409.
4. Sets `status` = waived and records `waived_by` (the calling admin) and the trimmed `waived_reason`.
5. Publishes a `beep.captain.activation_waived` realtime/audit event on the captain's channel capturing the before/after status.
6. Returns the updated `CaptainDailyActivation`.

**Use Cases:**
- Forgiving an activation fee for a captain as a goodwill or dispute resolution by a super-admin.

**Restrictions:**
- Super-admin role only; other roles receive 403.
- `reason` must be at least 10 characters after trimming.
- Only a `pending` record can be waived; any non-pending status (already `waived`, already `paid`, or `failed`) returns 409. Not idempotent: re-waiving an already-waived record returns 409.

200.description: Fee waived; the updated activation record

400.description: Reason is shorter than 10 characters

404.description: No activation record with this ID

409.description: Record is not pending (already waived, already paid, or failed) and cannot be waived

post.description:
Approve up to 100 pending captains in a single admin action, all with the same service scope.

**Features:**
- Runs each captain id through the full approval engine (document gate + state machine + `beep.captain.approved` event).
- Per-row independent processing: one bad id never aborts the batch.
- Optional `abriyah` flag grants Abriyah (shared-ride) access to every captain approved by this call.
- Optional `note` field is accepted but currently informational only.

**Behavior:**
1. Reject the call (400) if the id list is empty or has more than 100 items.
2. For each captain id, attempt engine approval with the requested scope.
3. An id that is missing, non-pending, or document-incomplete is recorded in `errors`, not returned as a 4xx.
4. Respond 200 with `succeeded`, `failed`, and per-failed-row `errors`.

**Use Cases:**
- Clearing a backlog of vetted captain applications from the Admin Dashboard.
- Onboarding a whole fleet straight onto Abriyah with `abriyah: true`.

**Restrictions:**
- Admin-only (riders are rejected with 403).
- List must be non-empty and at most 100 ids.
- `abriyah` defaults to false (taxi only) when omitted.

400.description: Empty list or more than 100 ids

401.description: Missing, invalid, or revoked bearer token

403.description: Authenticated as a rider (admin role required)

post.summary: Export trips as a JSON array
post.description:
Export trip rows matching a filter, as a flat JSON array for download or reporting.

**Features:**
- Filterable by `city_id`, `zone_id`, `trip_type`, `status`, and a request-time window (`from_date` / `to_date`, RFC3339).
- All filter fields are optional; omitting them exports across all dimensions.
- `limit` is clamped to `[1, 10_000]` and defaults to 1000 when omitted.

**Behavior:**
- Each row carries trip id, type, status, rider id, optional captain/zone ids, integer-IQD fare, distance in km, and request/completion timestamps.
- `captain_id`, `zone_id`, and `completed_at` are null until assigned/completed.

**Use Cases:**
- Pulling an operational trip dataset for a city or zone over a date range.

**Restrictions:**
- Admin-only (riders are rejected with 403).
- At most 10,000 rows are returned regardless of a larger requested limit.

401.description: Missing, invalid, or revoked bearer token

403.description: Authenticated as a rider (admin role required)

post.description:
Archive up to 50 zones in a single admin action.

**Features:**
- Per-row independent processing: one skipped zone never aborts the batch.
- On a successful archive, publishes a best-effort `beep.zone.archived` event (failure never fails the row).

**Behavior:**
1. Reject the call (400) if the id list is empty or has more than 50 items.
2. For each zone id, apply guards in order: not found, already archived, or has active trips / open rooms.
3. Any guard hit records a row error (e.g. `not found`, `already archived`, `has active trips or rooms`) instead of a 4xx.
4. Respond 200 with `succeeded`, `failed`, and per-failed-row `errors`.

**Use Cases:**
- Decommissioning several inactive service zones at once.

**Restrictions:**
- Admin-only (riders are rejected with 403).
- List must be non-empty and at most 50 ids.
- A zone with active trips or open rooms is skipped, not force-archived.

400.description: Empty list or more than 50 ids

401.description: Missing, invalid, or revoked bearer token

403.description: Authenticated as a rider (admin role required)

get.description:
Return the audit-log history for one captain as activity-feed rows.

**Features:**
- Reverse-chronological audit entries scoped to this captain (registration, approval, rejection, block/unblock, reconsider, and other tracked events).
- Each row carries an event type, human description, optional linked entity, and timestamp.
- Returns an empty list (not 404) for a captain with no audit history.

**Use Cases:**
- Show the captain's lifecycle timeline on the Captain Detail History tab.

Retrieve every operating city, active and inactive alike.

**Features:**
- Returns all cities with no filtering or pagination
- Includes inactive cities (those not yet activated for multi-city expansion)
- Each row carries IANA timezone (e.g. Asia/Baghdad) and ISO currency (e.g. IQD)

**Use Cases:**
- Populate the city picker in the Admin Dashboard
- Audit which cities are live before activating zones or trips

post.description:
Register a new operating city.

**Features:**
- Timezone defaults to Asia/Baghdad when omitted
- Currency defaults to IQD when omitted
- Active flag defaults per the repository when omitted

**Behavior:**
- Inserts a new city row and returns the persisted record with its generated UUID

**Restrictions:**
- Admin role required
- name and name_ar are required

400.description: Malformed JSON body (syntax error)

422.description: JSON body is missing a required field (e.g. name, name_ar) or has a wrong-typed field

get.description:
Fetch a single city record by its UUID.

**Returns:**
- Full city record: name, Arabic name, IANA timezone, ISO currency, and active flag
- Returns the city regardless of its active state

**Use Cases:**
- Display a city's settings before editing
- Resolve a city referenced by a zone or trip

put.description:
Partially update a city's mutable attributes.

**Updatable Fields:**
- name, name_ar, timezone, currency, active
- Every field is optional; omitted fields are left unchanged (partial update)

**Restrictions:**
- Admin role required

400.description: Malformed JSON body (syntax error)

422.description: JSON body has a wrong-typed field

post.description:
Turn a city on for the multi-city expansion (Phase 11).

**Behavior:**
1. Loads the city; 404 if it does not exist
2. Rejects with 409 if the city is already active (this is a guard, not a no-op idempotent return)
3. Sets active = true and persists
4. Writes an audit row and fans out a beep.city.activated ops event

**Use Cases:**
- Bring a new city (e.g. Erbil, Basra, Mosul) online so its zones and trip logic begin matching

**Restrictions:**
- Admin role required
- The active flip propagates through existing city_id query filters; no schema change

409.description: City is already active

post.description:
Turn a city off (Phase 11).

**Behavior:**
1. Loads the city; 404 if it does not exist
2. Rejects with 409 if the city is already inactive (guard, not a no-op)
3. Sets active = false and persists
4. Writes an audit row and fans out a beep.city.deactivated ops event

**Use Cases:**
- Suspend a city so its zones and trip logic stop matching new demand

**Restrictions:**
- Admin role required
- This endpoint only flips the active flag; it does not cancel in-flight trips

409.description: City is already inactive

get.description:
Return the All-Customers directory with optional filters and pagination.

**Features:**
- Optional `phone` substring filter and `blocked` boolean filter.
- Each row carries name, phone, gender, total trips, cancellation count, blocked flag, and created time.
- Paginated: `page` is 1-based (clamped to >= 1); `per_page` defaults to 50 and is clamped to 1-200. The response echoes the effective `page` and `per_page`.

**Use Cases:**
- Browse and search the customer directory in the admin dashboard.

Return the detail overview for one customer.

**Returns:**
- Name, phone, gender, blocked flag and block reason, total trips, average rating received and given, cancellation count, and created time.
- Phone is shown in full (admin view, not proxied).

**Use Cases:**
- Render the customer profile drawer in the admin dashboard.

post.description:
Block a customer account with a recorded reason.

**Behavior:**
1. Trims and validates `reason` is at least 10 characters (400 otherwise).
2. Blocks the customer only if currently unblocked; publishes a `customer.blocked` audit event.
3. Only sets `blocked = TRUE`; it does NOT touch trips, so existing trips run to completion. Enforcement of the block (e.g. rejecting the customer's next OTP login) is handled in the auth domain, not here.
4. A missing customer returns 404; an already-blocked customer returns 409.
5. Returns `{ ok: true }`.

**Use Cases:**
- Suspend an abusive or fraudulent customer.

**Restrictions:**
- Super-admin only (403 otherwise).
- `reason` must be >= 10 characters after trimming.

400.description: Reason shorter than 10 characters

409.description: Customer already blocked

put.description:
Override the stored gender for a customer (used to gate women-only Abriyah).

**Updatable Fields:**
- `gender` only; must be `m`, `f`, or `unset` (400 otherwise).

**Behavior:**
1. Validates the gender value.
2. Applies the override; a missing customer returns 404.
3. Publishes a `customer.gender_overridden` audit event with the previous and new values.
4. Returns `{ ok: true }`.

**Restrictions:**
- Super-admin only (403 otherwise).
- Gender must be one of `m` | `f` | `unset`.

400.description: Invalid gender value

get.description:
Return the audit-log history for one customer as activity-feed rows.

**Features:**
- Reverse-chronological audit entries scoped to this customer (blocks, gender overrides, and other tracked events).
- Each row carries an event type, description, optional linked entity, and timestamp.
- Returns an empty list (not 404) for a customer with no audit history.

**Use Cases:**

post.description:
Lift a block from a customer account.

**Behavior:**
1. Unblocks the customer only if currently blocked; publishes a `customer.unblocked` audit event.
2. A missing customer returns 404; a customer that is not blocked returns 409.
3. Returns `{ ok: true }`.

**Use Cases:**
- Restore access to a customer after review.

**Restrictions:**
- Super-admin only (403 otherwise).
- Takes no request body.

409.description: Customer is not blocked

get.description:
Return the most recent activity-feed rows, mapped from the audit log.

**Features:**
- Reverse-chronological highlights (newest first), each with an event type, human description, and optional linked entity.
- Only covers the last 24 hours: rows are filtered by `created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'`, so older activity never appears.
- `limit` is requested via the query param (defaults to 20) but is hard-clamped server-side to the range 1-20; the max returnable rows is 20 regardless of the requested value (e.g. `limit=50` still returns at most 20).

**Use Cases:**
- Populate the dashboard "recent activity" feed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max rows to return (defaults to 20); hard-capped at 20 even if a larger value is requested

get.description:
Return the 8 dashboard KPI cards plus yesterday deltas, computed in one query.

**Features:**
- Today-vs-now metrics: trips, completed, cancelled, active trips, open rooms, active captains, activations, and accrued activation fees (integer IQD).
- Includes `completed_yesterday` and `trips_yesterday` so the client can render deltas.
- "Today" is the Asia/Baghdad calendar day; counters roll at Baghdad midnight.

Return badge counts for the 4 Needs-Action tabs, excluding rows the calling admin dismissed.

**Features:**
- One count each for pending captains, flagged trips, expired rooms, and stuck items.
- `any_sla_breach` is true when at least one pending captain has waited more than 24h.
- The flagged-trips, expired-rooms, and stuck-items counts are per-admin: items this admin dismissed are not counted. The pending-captains count is global (it reflects the live approval queue) and is NOT per-admin, because pending captains cannot be dismissed.

Dismiss a Needs-Action item for the calling admin so it stops appearing in their counts and tabs.

1. Validates `item_type` is one of `flagged_trip`, `expired_room`, or `stuck_item` (400 otherwise).
2. Records a per-admin dismissal for the given `item_id`.
3. The item no longer shows in this admin's badge counts or tab lists; other admins are unaffected.
4. Returns `{ ok: true }`.

**Use Cases:**
- Clear an item the admin has already handled or judged not actionable.

**Restrictions:**
- Any admin may call this; the dismissal is scoped to the caller only.
- Pending captains cannot be dismissed (not an accepted `item_type`).

get.description:
Return the Needs-Action Tab 3 list: Abriyah rooms that expired within the last 24h.

**Features:**
- Each row carries zone name, room type, rider count at expiry, and open/expiry timestamps.
- Rows this admin has dismissed are excluded.

Return the Needs-Action Tab 2 list: trips flagged as long-running, late-cancelled, or low-rated.

**Features:**
- Each row carries the flag reason, trip type, captain/zone names, request time, status duration (minutes), and average stars.

- Implicitly scoped to the caller (taken from the bearer token subject); never returns another admin's preferences.

get.summary: List live Abriyah rooms for ops

Return live Abriyah room cards for the Operations Kanban.

**Features:**
- Filter by comma-separated `status` (defaults to open, locked, dispatched when omitted), `zone_id`, and `room_type`.
- Each card carries zone name, room type, status, current vs max riders, captain name, open time, and elapsed vs max wait (seconds).
- Not paginated; the default status set keeps the result to in-flight rooms.

**Use Cases:**
- Render the real-time Abriyah room Kanban, optionally scoped by zone or room type.

parameters.name: zone_id
parameters.description: Restrict to rooms in this zone

post.description:
Force-dispatch a locked Abriyah room (which already has a captain assigned).

**Behavior:**
1. Loads the room; a missing room returns 404.
2. Requires status `locked`; any other status returns 400.
3. Calls the room state machine's dispatch (guards status IN open,locked); a concurrent race surfaces as 400.
4. On success the room moves to `dispatched` and a `beep.room.dispatched` event (forced) is published.
5. Returns `{ ok: true }`.

**Use Cases:**
- Push a captain-assigned room into dispatch when auto-dispatch stalls.

**Restrictions:**
- Super-admin only (403 otherwise).

Authenticate a dashboard admin by email and password and mint a role-bearing JWT.

**Behavior:**
- Looks up the admin by email; an unknown email and a wrong password return the SAME 401 (the response never reveals whether the email exists).
- Rejects the login with 403 when the account is disabled.
- Verifies the password against the stored argon2 hash.
- Stamps `last_login_at` to now on success.

post.summary: Send a login OTP to a phone
post.description:
Issue a one-time passcode for phone-based login and enqueue it for delivery.

**Features:**
- Used by both riders and captains; the same code works for either verify endpoint.
- Generates a numeric code (configurable length), Argon2id-hashes it, and stores an active challenge.
- Delivery is durable: the plaintext code is pushed onto the `send_otp` Redis queue and sent by a background worker, so a 200 means enqueued, not yet delivered.

**Use Cases:**
- A rider or captain starts phone-based login and needs a fresh code sent to their device.
- The user requested to resend the code after the previous one expired or never arrived.

**Behavior:**
- Normalizes the phone: strips a leading `+` and requires 10-15 digits.
- Rate limited to a configured number of issuances per rolling 10-minute window per phone.
- Each new send creates a fresh challenge with its own expiry.
- The response includes `already_registered`: when true the phone already belongs to a rider or an active captain, so the client should branch to a Login (password) screen instead of continuing the signup form (which would 409 at register).

**Restrictions:**
- Phone must be 10-15 ASCII digits (a leading `+` is allowed and stripped); otherwise 400.
- Exceeding the per-phone send rate limit returns 400.

Report whether a phone already owns a rider and/or an active captain account, so the client can branch a single phone field to Login (ask password) vs Signup (send OTP + collect name) BEFORE the user fills out the signup form.

- `captain_exists` counts only non-archived captains (an archived captain may re-register).
- `registered = rider_exists || captain_exists`.
- Public, no auth. Does not send an OTP and is not rate limited; pair it with the phone field, then call `/api/auth/otp/send` only when proceeding.

**Note:** this reveals whether a phone is registered (account enumeration), which is the accepted trade-off for a clean signup/login branch in the apps.

get.description:
Resolve whether the authenticated captain has activated for the current Asia/Baghdad day.

**Returns:**
- `activated` -- true when an activation row exists for today, false otherwise.
- `activation` -- the full daily-activation record when activated (id, date, fee in integer IQD, status pending/paid/waived/failed, charge_error on a failed charge); null when not yet activated.

**Behavior:**
- The captain id is taken from the JWT subject; no path or query input.
- The day rolls over at Asia/Baghdad midnight, so a fresh day reads back `activated=false` until the captain taps Activate Today.

**Use Cases:**
- Captain App home screen deciding whether to show the Activate Today CTA or the active-for-today badge.
- Pre-check before letting the captain go online (the online toggle requires a same-day activation).

**Restrictions:**
- Requires a captain bearer token (the route is gated to role `captain`; a rider token is rejected with 403).
- The captain must exist and be `approved`; an unapproved captain is rejected with 403, an unknown captain with 404.

403.description: Token is not a captain role, or the captain is not approved

post.summary: Tap Activate Today and charge the daily fee
post.description:
Activate the authenticated captain for the current Asia/Baghdad day and collect the daily activation fee from the captain wallet.

**Features:**
- Idempotent per day: a re-tap of an already-activated day returns the existing row without re-charging.
- The fee is read from the `activation.daily_fee_iqd` setting (integer IQD), falling back to a built-in default when the setting is unset.
- Emits a real-time `beep.captain.activated_today` event to the captain WS session and best-effort updates the reports rollup with the post-charge status.

**Behavior:**
1. The captain id is taken from the JWT subject; the request body has no fields in v1.
2. A pending activation row is created idempotently for today (Asia/Baghdad).
3. The captain wallet is charged the fee: on success the row flips pending -> paid (collected_at set); on insufficient funds it flips pending -> failed (charge_error set) and the call returns 402 so the CTA persists for top-up and retry.
4. The response is re-fetched after the charge, so the returned status reflects `paid`.

**Restrictions:**
- Requires a captain bearer token (the route is gated to role `captain`; a rider token is rejected with 403).
- The captain must exist and be `approved`; an unapproved captain is rejected with 403, an unknown captain with 404.
- A failed charge (insufficient wallet balance) returns 402 PaymentRequired; the captain tops up the wallet and taps again.

Read the authenticated captain's own last-known location row.

- The captain app restoring its map pin and online state after a restart.
- Confirming a ping was persisted.

post.description:
Record the captain's current GPS position and fan it out in real time.

**Features:**
- Upserts the captain's last-known location row (WGS-84 longitude/latitude).
- A ping implies presence, so it sets the captain `online = true`.
- Fans the position out over Redis to the captain's own pin channel and the admin live map; if the captain is on an active trip, it also pushes to that trip's channel so the rider sees the car move.
- No audit row is written per ping (real-time fan-out only).

**Behavior:**
1. Validate coordinates (longitude in [-180, 180], latitude in [-90, 90]).
2. Upsert the location row. On a transient DB write failure the ping is buffered to the Redis `queue:ping_flush` list and the error is surfaced so the app retries.
3. Publish the new position to the captain, admin-ops, and (if applicable) active-trip channels.

- Requires a captain JWT (captain-role middleware).
- Out-of-range coordinates are rejected with 400.

403.description: Authenticated token is not a captain

post.description:
Flush the GPS pings the captain app buffered while offline.

**Features:**
- Accepts an ordered batch of pings collected during a connectivity gap.
- Applies a last-known interpolation policy: only the final ping in the batch is stored.
- Storing that ping runs the same path as a live ping: it sets the captain online and fans the position out to the captain pin channel, the admin live map, and any active-trip channel.

**Behavior:**
1. Take the last entry in `pings` (an empty array is rejected with 400).
2. Validate its coordinates (longitude in [-180, 180], latitude in [-90, 90]).
3. Upsert and fan out exactly as a single live ping would.

**Restrictions:**
- Requires a captain JWT (captain-role middleware).
- An empty `pings` array or out-of-range coordinates are rejected with 400.

400.description: Empty pings array or out-of-range coordinates

403.description: Authenticated token is not a captain

delete.description:
Permanently delete the authenticated captain's own account and personal data (App Store guideline 5.1.1(v): in-app account deletion).

**Password required:** the request body must carry the captain's current password (`{"password": "..."}`). It is verified server-side against the stored hash; there is no code path that deletes an account without a successful password check. A request that is not valid JSON, carries no `Content-Type: application/json`, or omits the `password` field is rejected by the framework before any deletion happens (415 / 422 / 400 -- see the status codes below). Those rejections come from axum itself, so their bodies are PLAIN TEXT, not this API's `{"error": ...}` envelope; clients must not try to parse them as JSON.

**Behavior:**
1. Captain-only (enforced by captain-role middleware).
2. The live captain account for the token subject is loaded; if there is none, or it is already archived, 404.
3. The supplied `password` is verified against the stored hash through the SAME throttled gate as captain login: a locked account is refused with 429 and a blocked one with 403 before the password is looked at, a wrong password answers 401 with body `{"error":"wrong_password"}` and counts toward the lockout (5 failures -> locked for 15 minutes), and a correct one clears the failure counter. Nothing is deleted unless the password is correct.
4. Refused while a trip is in flight (accepted or in_progress) -- finish or cancel it first, else 409.
5. The account is archived and anonymized: phone, name, vehicle plate, national id, push token, and password hash are scrubbed, and the captain can no longer log in. The phone number and plate are freed, so the same person may register a fresh account later.
6. De-identified trip, activation, and payment records are retained where legally required (see the privacy policy).

**Client contract:**
- Only 204 and 404 end the session. On 204 (or 404, meaning already deleted), discard the stored JWT and return the user to the signed-out screen. Deletion is irreversible.
- A 401 is ambiguous by status alone, so branch on the BODY. `{"error":"wrong_password"}` means the password was rejected but the session is still valid: keep the user signed in, stay on the delete screen, and show an inline error on the password field. ANY other 401 (the bare body from the auth middleware, or `{"error":"unauthorized"}`) means the token itself is dead -- sign the user out normally, exactly as on every other endpoint.
- 400 / 415 / 422 are framework-level body rejections (malformed JSON syntax, missing `Content-Type: application/json`, missing or mistyped `password`) whose bodies are plain text, not the `{"error": ...}` envelope. 409 means an active trip is blocking the delete. 429 means the account is temporarily locked after repeated wrong passwords; the same lockout as login applies here. All of these leave the session and the account untouched.
- The captain's current token is not server-revoked and remains technically valid until it expires; after a 204 always discard it client-side immediately.

204.description: Account deleted; discard the token and sign the user out

400.description: Malformed JSON syntax in the body (axum rejection; PLAIN-TEXT body, not the `{"error": ...}` envelope). Nothing was deleted

401.description: Branch on the body, not the status. Body `{"error":"wrong_password"}` = the password was wrong: keep the session and show an inline error on the password field. Any other 401 body (bare text from the auth middleware, or `{"error":"unauthorized"}`) = the bearer token is missing, invalid or expired: sign the user out

403.description: The token is not a captain token, or the captain account is blocked

404.description: No live captain account for the token subject (already deleted)

409.description: The captain has an active trip; finish or cancel it first

415.description: No `Content-Type: application/json` on the request (axum rejection; PLAIN-TEXT body). Nothing was deleted

422.description: Body is valid JSON but `password` is missing or not a string (axum rejection; PLAIN-TEXT body). Nothing was deleted

429.description: Too many wrong passwords: the account is temporarily locked (same 5-attempt / 15-minute lockout as login)

put.description:
Restate the authenticated captain's own car and re-grade it. Captain role; the record is taken from the token `sub`, so a captain can only ever edit their own car.

Registration used to be the only moment a car could be described, and the star grade it produces sets the fare: star 1/2/3 price at 500/700/1000 IQD per km. A captain who typed 2109 for 2019, or picked the wrong model, was stuck on the wrong grade permanently -- the only lever was `PUT /api/captains/{id}/star`, which is super-admin-only AND pins the grade. This endpoint fixes the car instead of overriding the symptom.

**A self-service edit can lower your grade, but it cannot raise it on its own.** The star this route produces comes from an unverified self-declaration -- nothing here re-checks the `car_registration` document, and `car_plate` (which is not editable) does not constrain make/model -- so a re-grade that would move the star UP is stored as a REQUEST: the description and the catalog ids are saved and returned, `star` stays where it was, and the captain is queued for an operator to check against their registration document. A re-grade that keeps the star the same or lowers it applies immediately, because it costs the platform nothing. Read `star` back off the 200 body: if it did not move, the raise is pending review, not lost.

**Updatable fields:** `car_make` and `car_model` (required, non-empty), `car_color`, `car_brand_id`, `car_model_id`, `car_year`. Field names and meanings are identical to the vehicle half of `POST /api/captains/register`.

**This is a PUT, not a PATCH:** `car_color` and `car_year` are CLEARED when omitted. In particular, omitting `car_year` drops the captain to star 1, because a car with no year clears no age gate. Always send the full block. `car_brand_id`/`car_model_id` are the exception -- they are stored as whatever the grader RESOLVED, so omitting them re-derives the match from the free-text make/model rather than clearing it; send the ids explicitly to change the catalog identification.

**Behavior:**
1. Refuse with 409 while the captain is on an `accepted` or `in_progress` trip. The rider is looking at a make, model and colour on their screen; changing the car underneath them mid-ride is not acceptable. The body carries `trip_id` so the app can deep-link to the blocking trip.
2. Validate: `car_make`/`car_model` non-empty, `car_year` in 1970..=2100, that a supplied `car_brand_id` exists in the catalog, and -- when `car_model_id` is sent -- that the model exists and, if `car_brand_id` is sent too, that the model really belongs to that brand. A mismatched pair is rejected rather than silently stored, because it would grade the captain as a car they did not pick.
3. Re-grade through the same classifier registration uses, and persist the catalog ids the grader resolved. `star` moves only if the new grade is not higher than the current one. If an admin has PINNED this captain's grade (`star_overridden_at` is set), `star` is left exactly as the admin decided in either direction and only the description changes -- a captain editing their own row never silently undoes a deliberate override.
4. Publish `beep.captain.vehicle_changed` (audit; `star_review_requested` says whether a raise is now waiting on a human) and return the updated captain.

**Restrictions:**
- Captain role. `car_plate` cannot be changed here: the plate is the car's legal identity, is unique across captains, and is on the rider's screen and the trip record.
- A car that matches no catalog model is graded on model year alone and is capped at star 2; send `car_model_id` to be gradable above that.

200.description: Vehicle updated. Re-graded unless the star is pinned or the re-grade would raise it (then the raise is queued for review); returns the captain

400.description: Blank car_make/car_model, car_year outside 1970..=2100, an unknown car_brand_id, an unknown car_model_id, or a car_model_id that does not belong to the supplied car_brand_id

404.description: No live captain for the token subject

409.description: The captain is on an active trip. Body is `{"error":"finish the active trip before changing your vehicle", "trip_id":"<uuid>"}`

put.description:
Set the captain's online availability, enforcing the daily activation gate.

**Updatable Fields:**
- `online` (bool) -- the only field; sets whether the captain is available for dispatch.

**Behavior:**
1. When going online, the daily activation gate is checked: an Asia/Baghdad-dated `captain_daily_activations` row for today in `pending`, `paid`, or `waived` status must exist, otherwise 403.
2. When going offline, the captain must not be on an active trip: an `accepted` or `in_progress` trip is refused with 409. The rider's live car is driven by this captain's pings, so a mid-ride offline toggle would freeze the car on the rider's map with no explanation. Finish or cancel the trip first.
3. Persist the new online flag on the captain's location row.
4. When going offline, publish a fade-pin message `{event: "captain_location", captain_id, online: false}` to the captain's own channel and the admin live map so subscribers drop the pin.

**Restrictions:**
- Requires a captain JWT (captain-role middleware).
- Going online without a same-day activation row is rejected with 403.
- Going offline while on an active trip is rejected with 409 (body carries `trip_id`).

403.description: Forbidden. Body is `{"error":"activation_required"}` when the captain is approved but has no successful daily activation for today (top up / activate first); `{"error":"forbidden"}` when the token is not a captain.

409.description: Cannot go offline while on an active trip. Body is `{"error":"finish the active trip before going offline", "trip_id":"<uuid>"}` -- deep-link the captain to that trip.

post.description:
Self-service captain registration from the Captain App. Public, no auth. Creates a captain in the `pending` status awaiting admin review.

The body now requires a verified `ticket` (from POST /api/auth/otp/verify with purpose 'register') and a chosen `password`. The phone must be proven via that ticket before the account is created, and the password is Argon2id-hashed before storage.

**Features:**
- Normalizes the phone (strips a leading '+', requires 10-15 digits) before storing.
- Gender is validated to 'm' or 'f' and is locked after creation.
- Publishes `beep.captain.registered` and enqueues an admin review notification.

**Behavior:**
1. Consume the verified 'register' ticket for this phone; reject if invalid or expired.
2. Validate gender ('m' | 'f') and normalize the phone.
3. Reject if the phone is already registered.
4. Reject if the car plate is already registered.
5. Hash the password and insert the captain as `pending`, then emit the registration event.
6. Mint an onboarding captain JWT and return it alongside the captain.

**Onboarding token (since 2026-06-16):** the 201 body is the `Captain` object plus a `token` field (a captain JWT for this `pending` captain). Use it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to upload the 5 required documents (`POST /api/captains/{id}/documents`, etc.) and to poll `GET /api/captains/{id}` until `approved` -- no separate login is needed. The token is onboarding-scoped in effect: every operational endpoint (go online, trip-queue, accept/start/ complete, location, proxy, multi-stop) independently returns 403 until the captain is approved, and document/self-read endpoints enforce that the token owns the `{id}` it acts on.

**Restrictions:**
- Phone and car plate must be unique across all captains.
- `city_id` must reference an existing city. This is enforced at INSERT time by the database FK, not a pre-insert existence check: any DB constraint violation on insert is coerced to a 404, so a missing city is the typical (but not the only possible) cause.
- No authentication required, but a valid registration ticket is mandatory.

201.description: Captain registered in pending status, with an onboarding token

400.description: Invalid gender or malformed phone number

404.description: A DB constraint failed on insert (typically a non-existent referenced city)

409.description: Phone or car plate already registered

get.description:
Retrieve a single captain's full lifecycle record by ID. A captain may read ONLY their own record (token `sub` == `{id}`); any admin role may read any captain. Other tokens get 403.

**Returns:**
- The complete captain record: identity, vehicle details, `city_id`, `status` (pending | approved | rejected | blocked), rejection/blocked reasons, approval metadata, `avg_rating`, trip and cancellation counts, and the optimistic-lock `version`.
- `national_id` and `car_color` are nullable and may be omitted.

**Use Cases:**
- The Captain App loading the signed-in captain's own profile and status.
- The Admin Dashboard opening a captain detail view.

403.description: Token is neither this captain nor an admin

delete.description:
Soft-delete a captain. Super-admin only.

A captain is referenced by trips, ratings, rooms and reports, so they are not physically removed; instead they are moved to the terminal `archived` status (`status = 'archived'`, stamping `archived_at`/`archived_by`). Their ride history is preserved.

**Behavior:**
1. Load the captain; 404 if not found.
2. Pre-check the captain is not already archived; 400 otherwise. The conditional UPDATE re-guards, so a concurrent archive yields a 409.
3. Mark archived, publish `beep.captain.archived`, enqueue a force-cancel job for any active trips (reason `captain_archived`), and notify the captain.

**Effects:**
- The captain disappears from the default `GET /api/captains` list (still retrievable with `?status=archived`).
- The captain can no longer log in (the login gate only admits `approved`/`pending`).

**Restrictions:**
- Requires the `super_admin` role.
- Already-archived captains cannot be archived again.

400.description: Captain is already archived (pre-check)

409.description: Captain was archived concurrently (optimistic-lock loss)

post.description:
Grant a captain Abriyah (shared-ride) access, setting `abriyah_status = approved` and clearing any stored reason. The captain then sees and can accept Abriyah rooms. Admin-only.

**Behavior:**
1. Set `abriyah_status = approved` from ANY current state; 404 if no captain has this id.
2. Publish `beep.captain.abriyah_approved` and enqueue an `Abriyah access approved` captain notification.

**Use Cases:**
- Widening an already-approved captain's scope after they were approved as taxi-only.

**Restrictions:**
- Admin role. There is no request to answer first: this is a plain grant, not a review decision.

200.description: Abriyah access granted; returns the captain

post.description:
Take Abriyah (shared-ride) access away from a captain, setting `abriyah_status = none` and clearing any stored reason. The captain keeps normal taxi work. Admin-only.

**Behavior:**
1. Set `abriyah_status = none` from ANY current state; 404 if no captain has this id.
2. Publish `beep.captain.abriyah_revoked` and enqueue an `Abriyah access removed` captain notification.
3. The matching gates read `abriyah_status` on every offer, so Abriyah rooms stop being offered immediately. A room the captain is already assigned to is not disturbed.

**Use Cases:**
- Pulling a captain off shared rides after complaints, without blocking their account.

**Restrictions:**
- Admin role. Idempotent: revoking a captain who never had access leaves them at `none`.

200.description: Abriyah access revoked; returns the captain

post.description:
Approve a captain currently in the `pending` status, transitioning them to `approved`, and pick their service scope in the same call. Admin-only.

**Behavior:**
1. Load the captain; 404 if not found.
2. Pre-check the current status is `pending`; if not, reject as an invalid transition (400). The conditional UPDATE also re-guards on `pending`, so a concurrent status change between the pre-check and the UPDATE yields a 409 (optimistic-lock loss).
3. Require all five required document types on file via the document gate; otherwise reject as incomplete (400).
4. Mark approved (records the approving admin from the bearer token). When `abriyah` is true the SAME statement sets `abriyah_status = approved`, so scope and approval cannot diverge.
5. Publish `beep.captain.approved` and enqueue ONE captain notification (`Account approved`) -- granting Abriyah here does NOT add a second push.

**Use Cases:**
- Operator clearing a captain from the pending queue once documents check out.
- Onboarding a captain straight onto Abriyah shared rides without a separate request/approval round-trip.

**Restrictions:**
- The body is OPTIONAL. Omitting it entirely (no body, no content-type) means `abriyah: false` -- taxi only.
- Only `pending` captains can be approved (idempotent re-approval is not allowed).
- All required documents (driver_license, car_registration, captain_selfie, national_id_front, national_id_back) must be present.

requestBody.description: Optional service scope. Omit the body for taxi only; send `{"abriyah": true}` to also grant Abriyah shared-ride access.

400.description: Documents incomplete, captain is not in pending status (pre-check), or a supplied body is not valid JSON

403.description: Authenticated as a rider (admin role required)

409.description: Captain left the pending status concurrently (optimistic-lock loss / illegal transition)

post.description:
Block a captain currently in the `approved` status, transitioning them to `blocked`. Super-admin only.

**Behavior:**
1. Load the captain; 404 if not found.
2. Pre-check the current status is `approved`; if not, reject as an invalid transition (400). The conditional UPDATE re-guards on `approved`, so a concurrent status change after the pre-check yields a 409 (optimistic-lock loss).
3. Mark blocked with the supplied reason and publish `beep.captain.blocked`.
4. Enqueue a force-cancel job for the captain's active trips (reason `captain_blocked`) and a captain notification (push sign-out cue).

**Use Cases:**
- Removing a misbehaving captain from service and cancelling their in-flight trips.

**Restrictions:**
- Requires the `super_admin` role.
- Only `approved` captains can be blocked.

400.description: Captain is not in approved status (pre-check)

409.description: Captain left the approved status concurrently (optimistic-lock loss / illegal transition)

get.description:
List all of a captain's uploaded documents. A captain may list ONLY their own (token `sub` == `{id}`); any admin role may list any. Other tokens get 403.

**Returns:**
- One entry per uploaded document with `doc_type`, `url`, and `uploaded_at`.
- When managed storage is configured, each `url` is a short-lived presigned view URL rather than the raw stored object key; a presign failure falls back to the raw stored value.
- An empty array when the captain has uploaded nothing.

**Use Cases:**
- The Admin Dashboard rendering a captain's documents during review.
- The Captain App showing which documents are on file.

200.description: The captain's documents (presigned view URLs when storage is managed)

403.description: Token is neither this captain nor an admin

post.summary: Upload or replace a captain document
post.description:
Persist (or replace) one of a captain's required documents. A captain may write ONLY their own documents (token `sub` == `{id}`); any admin role may write any. Other tokens get 403.

**Features:**
- Upserts by document type, so re-submitting a type replaces the prior reference.
- Accepts either the `object_key` from the presigned-upload flow (preferred) or a full `url` (bring-your-own).
- When managed storage is configured, the stored object key is returned back as a short-lived presigned view URL rather than the raw key.

**Behavior:**
1. Validate `doc_type` against the allowed set.
2. Verify the captain exists.
3. Choose the stored reference: non-empty `object_key` first, else non-empty `url`.
4. Upsert the document and return it with a resolvable `url`.

**Restrictions:**
- `doc_type` must be one of: driver_license, car_registration, captain_selfie, national_id_front, national_id_back.
- Exactly one of `object_key` or `url` (non-empty) must be provided, else the request is rejected.

200.description: Document stored; `url` is a presigned view URL when storage is managed

400.description: Invalid doc_type, or neither object_key nor url provided

403.description: Token is neither this captain nor an admin

get.description:
Report whether a captain has uploaded every document type required for approval. A captain may query ONLY their own (token `sub` == `{id}`); any admin role may query any. Other tokens get 403.

**Returns:**
- `complete`: true only when all required types are present.
- `uploaded`: the document types currently on file.
- `missing`: the required types not yet uploaded.
- Required types are: driver_license, car_registration, captain_selfie, national_id_front, national_id_back.
- An unknown captain ID yields an empty `uploaded` list and all types in `missing` (no 404).

**Use Cases:**
- The Captain App showing the captain which documents are still outstanding.
- The dashboard gauging whether a captain is ready for approval.

200.description: Completeness summary (complete flag, uploaded and missing types)

403.description: Token is neither this captain nor an admin

post.summary: Mint a presigned document upload URL
post.description:
Mint a short-lived presigned PUT URL so the client can upload one document directly to storage, bypassing this API. A captain may mint ONLY for their own documents (token `sub` == `{id}`); any admin role may mint for any. Other tokens get 403.

**Features:**
- Returns `upload_url` (presigned PUT target), `object_key`, and `expires_in` (seconds until the URL expires).
- The client PUTs the raw image bytes to `upload_url` directly, then persists the document via `POST /api/captains/{id}/documents` with the returned `object_key`.

**Behavior:**
1. Validate `doc_type` against the allowed set.
2. Verify the captain exists.
3. Ask the storage backend to presign an upload target for this captain and document type.

**Restrictions:**
- `doc_type` must be one of: driver_license, car_registration, captain_selfie, national_id_front, national_id_back.
- The returned URL is short-lived; upload before `expires_in` elapses.

400.description: Invalid doc_type

403.description: Token is neither this captain nor an admin

500.description: Storage backend failed to presign the upload URL

get.summary: Get a presigned view URL for a document
get.description:
Mint a short-lived presigned GET URL to view one specific captain document. Admin-only.

**Returns:**
- `view_url` (presigned GET URL) and `expires_in` (300 seconds).
- Open `view_url` to render the stored image during admin review.

**Behavior:**
1. Validate `doc_type` against the allowed set.
2. Locate the captain's document of that type; 404 if absent.
3. Presign a GET URL for the stored object.

**Use Cases:**
- Operator inspecting a specific document (e.g. driver_license) before approving.

parameters.name: doc_type
parameters.description: Document type: driver_license | car_registration | captain_selfie | national_id_front | national_id_back

200.description: Presigned view URL valid for 300 seconds

400.description: Invalid doc_type

403.description: Authenticated as a rider (admin role required)

404.description: Captain has no document of this type

500.description: Storage backend failed to presign the view URL

get.description:
Summarise a captain's earnings over a rolling period, net of the daily activation fee.

**Returns:**
- `gross_iqd`: sum of completed-trip fares since the period start (integer IQD).
- `activation_fee_iqd`: a single flat activation fee (2000 IQD) subtracted when gross is positive, else 0.
- `net_iqd`: gross minus the activation fee.
- `trip_count` and the echoed `period`.
- Period windows are rolling from now: `today`/`day` = last 24h, `week` = last 7d, `month` = last 30d. The activation fee is exact only for `today`; over week/month it is illustrative (a single fee, not per-day) in v1.

**Use Cases:**
- Captain app earnings dashboard for today, this week, or this month.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Rolling window: today | week | month (defaults to today)

400.description: Period is not one of today, week, month

get.description:
List a captain's completed trips within a rolling period, for an itemised earnings breakdown.

**Returns:**
- `items`: each completed trip the captain finished in the window, with its fare and supporting detail (integer IQD).
- The echoed `captain_id` and `period`.
- Period windows are rolling from now: `today`/`day` = last 24h, `week` = last 7d, `month` = last 30d.

**Use Cases:**
- Captain app drilling from the earnings summary into the underlying trips.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Rolling window: today | week | month (defaults to today)

200.description: Per-trip earnings history for the period

400.description: Period is not one of today, week, month

delete.description:
Hard-delete an ALREADY-ARCHIVED captain and their personal data, in one transaction. Super-admin only. This is the irreversible second step after the soft-delete (`DELETE /api/captains/{id}`), and is what frees the captain's identity completely (so the same phone/plate can be re-registered with a clean slate, leaving no archived ghost rows behind).

**What is removed:** the captain row plus (via cascade) their daily activations, uploaded document rows, location pings, and leaderboard rollup; their ratings (given and received); and their assignment to any room.

**What is PRESERVED:** their trips are detached (`captain_id` set to NULL), so trip and financial-ledger (transactions/revenue) history is kept intact and reports are not rewritten. Uploaded document image objects in storage are left in place (orphaned, no longer referenced).

**Behavior:**
1. Load the captain; 404 if not found.
2. Require `status = 'archived'`; 400 otherwise (archive first via `DELETE /api/captains/{id}`).
3. Purge in a transaction; on a concurrent change that leaves no archived row, 404.

**Restrictions:**
- Requires the `super_admin` role.
- Only archived captains can be purged. A live captain must be archived first.

400.description: Captain is not archived (archive it first)

404.description: No captain with this ID (or it was purged concurrently)

post.description:
Reset a captain currently in the `rejected` status back to `pending` for another review. Super-admin only.

**Behavior:**
1. Load the captain; 404 if not found.
2. Pre-check the current status is `rejected`; if not, reject as an invalid transition (400). The conditional UPDATE re-guards on `rejected`, so a concurrent status change after the pre-check yields a 409 (optimistic-lock loss).
3. Transition back to `pending`. Audit-only: no public event is published.

**Use Cases:**
- Giving a previously rejected captain a second chance after they re-submit documents.

**Restrictions:**
- Requires the `super_admin` role.
- Only `rejected` captains can be reconsidered.

400.description: Captain is not in rejected status (pre-check)

409.description: Captain left the rejected status concurrently (optimistic-lock loss / illegal transition)

post.description:
Reject a captain currently in the `pending` status with a coded reason, transitioning them to `rejected`. Admin-only.

**Behavior:**
1. Validate `reason` against the allowed reason codes; otherwise reject (400).
2. Load the captain; 404 if not found.
3. Pre-check the current status is `pending`; if not, reject as an invalid transition (400). The conditional UPDATE re-guards on `pending`, so a concurrent status change after the pre-check yields a 409 (optimistic-lock loss).
4. Persist the reason and optional comment, publish `beep.captain.rejected`, and enqueue a captain notification (the comment, if any, is used as the notification body).

**Use Cases:**
- Operator declining a captain whose documents or vehicle do not pass review.

**Restrictions:**
- `reason` must be one of: documents_invalid, vehicle_unfit, identity_mismatch, existing_account, other.
- Only `pending` captains can be rejected.

400.description: Invalid reason code, or captain is not in pending status (pre-check)

403.description: Authenticated as a rider (admin role required)

409.description: Captain left the pending status concurrently (optimistic-lock loss / illegal transition)

put.summary: Set or release a captain's car star grade
put.description:
Set a captain's car star grade to 1, 2, or 3 (3 = nicest) by hand, or send `{"star": null}` to release it. Super-admin only. Admins grade the car by eye at approval, and may change the grade anytime afterward (car upgraded, or a mis-grade). The grade drives normal-trip matching (a rider who requests star N is offered to captains graded N, widening to higher grades after `dispatch.star_widen_after_seconds`) and sets the per-km fare the captain earns: star 1/2/3 price at 500/700/1000 IQD per km. Abriyah ignores the star grade entirely.

**Setting a star PINS it.** A hand-set grade stamps `star_overridden_at`, which exempts the captain from automatic re-grading: `PUT /api/captain/me/vehicle` and `PUT /api/captains/{id}/vehicle` will both change that captain's car description and catalog ids from then on but leave `star` exactly where you put it. That is the point (a captain must not be able to undo your decision), but it means a pin is a standing decision, not a one-off nudge -- reach for `PUT /api/captains/{id}/vehicle` instead when the car *description* is what is wrong, and only pin when you are overruling the classifier itself.

**Releasing the pin: `{"star": null}`.** This is the ONLY way out of a pin. It clears `star_overridden_at` AND immediately re-grades the captain from their stored car through the same classifier registration uses, so the row never sits unpinned at a stale hand-set grade. Use it once the reason for the override is gone (the car was corrected, or the classifier was fixed). Either form also clears any pending `star_review_requested_at`: you have now looked at the car and answered.

**Behavior:**
1. With a `star`: validate it is 1, 2, or 3 (400 otherwise), write it, stamp `star_overridden_at`, clear `star_review_requested_at`.
2. With `null`: re-grade from the stored `car_brand_id`/`car_model_id`/`car_make`/`car_model`/`car_year`, write the computed grade, clear both flags.
3. 404 if no live captain has this id.
4. Publish `beep.captain.star_changed` (audit, payload carries the resulting `star` and whether it is now `pinned`) and return the updated captain.

**Restrictions:** requires the `super_admin` role.

200.description: Star pinned, or released and re-graded; returns the updated captain (read `star` and `star_overridden_at` back off it)

400.description: star must be 1, 2, or 3 (or null to release the pin)

post.description:
Restore a captain currently in the `blocked` status back to `approved`. Super-admin only.

**Behavior:**
1. Load the captain; 404 if not found.
2. Pre-check the current status is `blocked`; if not, reject as an invalid transition (400). The conditional UPDATE re-guards on `blocked`, so a concurrent status change after the pre-check yields a 409 (optimistic-lock loss).
3. Transition back to `approved`. Audit-only: no public event is published.

**Use Cases:**
- Reinstating a captain after a block is resolved.

**Restrictions:**
- Requires the `super_admin` role.
- Only `blocked` captains can be unblocked.

400.description: Captain is not in blocked status (pre-check)

409.description: Captain left the blocked status concurrently (optimistic-lock loss / illegal transition)

put.description:
The support-desk counterpart to `PUT /api/captain/me/vehicle`: restate a captain's car by id and re-grade it. Super-admin only, the same guard as `PUT /api/captains/{id}/star`.

Exists because the captain-facing route cannot always be used: the captain may be on the phone with support rather than in the app, may have already been pinned to a wrong grade, or may simply not understand which field is wrong. The star grade sets the per-km fare, so a mis-graded car is a money bug with no other operator-side fix that does not permanently pin the captain out of automatic re-grading.

**Updatable fields:** identical to the self-service route -- `car_make` and `car_model` (required, non-empty), `car_color`, `car_brand_id`, `car_model_id`, `car_year`.

**This is a PUT, not a PATCH:** `car_color` and `car_year` are CLEARED when omitted; omitting `car_year` drops the captain to star 1. `car_brand_id`/`car_model_id` do NOT clear -- they are stored as whatever the grader resolved, which for a body with no ids is whatever the free-text make/model fuzzy-matches, so re-sending the same free text re-derives the same match. Send the ids explicitly to change the catalog identification.

**This route re-grades in BOTH directions**, unlike the captain-facing one, which can only lower a grade on its own and queues a raise for review. You are the review: a super-admin has the registration document and the call in front of them, so a raise applied here needs no second pair of eyes, and doing so also clears any `star_review_requested_at` the captain had raised.

**Behavior:**
1. Validate exactly as the self-service route does: non-empty make/model, `car_year` in 1970..=2100, a real `car_brand_id`, a real `car_model_id`, and a `car_brand_id` that the model actually belongs to.
2. Re-grade through the same classifier, up or down. A PINNED grade (`star_overridden_at` set) is still preserved: correcting the description does not silently discard an earlier deliberate override. To make the grade move on a pinned captain, release the pin with `PUT /api/captains/{id}/star` `{"star": null}` -- that clears `star_overridden_at` and re-grades from the stored car in one call. (Sending a number to that route re-pins rather than releasing.)
3. Publish `beep.captain.vehicle_changed` (audit) and return the updated captain.

**Deliberately NOT guarded against an in-flight trip**, unlike the captain-facing route. A support ticket arrives precisely while the captain is working, and an operator who cannot touch the record until the captain is idle has no lever at all; the operator also has the context the captain lacks (they are on the call). The captain-side guard stays because a captain editing mid-ride has neither that context nor a reason that cannot wait.

**Restrictions:**
- Requires the `super_admin` role. `car_plate` cannot be changed here.
- 404 for an unknown captain, and for one whose account has been archived (a self-deleted record is anonymized and must read as no account).

200.description: Vehicle updated (and re-graded in either direction unless pinned); returns the captain

400.description: Blank car_make/car_model, car_year outside 1970..=2100, an unknown car_brand_id, an unknown car_model_id, or a car_model_id that does not belong to the supplied car_brand_id

404.description: No live captain with this ID

get.description:
Return a page of the trip's chat messages, oldest-first within the page. Readable by either participant even after the trip is completed or cancelled. Fetching also marks the counterparty's messages as read and fans out a `chat_read` receipt.

**Pagination:** omit `before` for the newest page; then request again with the oldest returned message's `created_at` as `before` to walk backwards. `has_more` is true when older messages remain.

**Restrictions:** any valid rider or captain JWT; the caller must be this trip's rider or assigned captain.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return messages older than this RFC3339 timestamp

403.description: Caller is not this trip's rider or assigned captain, or no captain is assigned yet

post.description:
Send a message on a trip's chat thread. The caller must be a participant of the trip: the rider who owns it, or the captain assigned to it. For Abriyah shared rides each rider has their own trip, so this is always a 1:1 rider<->captain thread with the shared captain.

**Behavior:**
- Persists the message, fans it out over the `rt:chat:trip:{id}` WebSocket channel, and enqueues an offline FCM push to the counterparty.
- The body is trimmed; empty or >2000-character bodies are rejected.

**Restrictions:**
- Any valid rider or captain JWT; the caller must be this trip's rider or assigned captain.
- Chat is only open while the trip is active (`accepted` or `in_progress`). Before a captain is assigned or after the trip is terminal, sending is rejected.

400.description: Empty or too-long body

403.description: Caller is not this trip's rider or assigned captain, or no captain is assigned yet

409.description: Chat is closed (trip is not active)

get.description:
Reports that the process is alive without touching any dependency.

**Returns:**
- `status`: always the literal "ok".
- `version`: the running `beeb` crate version (semver), useful for confirming the deployed build.

**Behavior:**
- Pure in-process check: does NOT query Postgres or Redis, so a slow or down dependency cannot make this fail.
- Always returns 200 while the process can handle requests.
- No authentication required.

**Use Cases:**
- Kubernetes / orchestrator liveness probe (restart on failure).
- Quick "is the API up" smoke test.
- For load-balancer routing decisions use `/api/health/ready` instead, which also checks dependencies.

Reports whether the instance can actually serve traffic by probing its dependencies.

**Returns:**
- `status`: "ready" when both checks pass, "not_ready" when either fails.
- `database`: `true` when a Postgres `SELECT 1` succeeded.
- `redis`: `true` when Redis answered a `PING`.

**Behavior:**
- Runs a Postgres `SELECT 1` and a Redis `PING` on each call; any error (including failure to acquire a Redis connection) marks that dependency as not ready.
- Returns 200 only when database AND redis are both reachable; returns 503 if either is down.
- The same JSON body is returned for both 200 and 503, so the per-dependency booleans can be inspected on failure.
- No authentication required.

**Use Cases:**
- Kubernetes readiness probe / load-balancer gating: route traffic away from this instance until it recovers.
- Diagnosing which dependency is degraded via the `database` and `redis` flags.

200.description: Ready to serve: both Postgres and Redis reachable

503.description: Not ready: Postgres or Redis unreachable

post.summary: Register or clear my FCM push token
post.description:
Store (or remove) the caller's FCM device token used for push notification delivery.

**Features:**
- Works for both riders and captains: the token is written to the row matching the JWT role (the `users` table for a rider, the `captains` table for a captain).
- Sending `{"fcm_token": null}` (or omitting the field) clears the stored token -- call this on logout to stop notifications.

**Behavior:**
1. Resolve the account from the token subject and role.
2. For role `rider`, set the token on the existing rider record; for role `captain`, set it on the existing captain record (a plain UPDATE -- it never inserts a new row, and returns 404 when no row matches).
3. Return 204 No Content on success (no response body).

**Restrictions:**
- Only the `rider` and `captain` roles are supported; any other role is rejected with 403.
- The token is always set for the authenticated caller; there is no way to set another account's token.

204.description: Token stored or cleared; no response body

403.description: Token role is neither rider nor captain

404.description: No account exists for the token subject

get.description:
List every saved payment method (cards and wallet) belonging to the authenticated rider or captain.

**Features:**
- Scoped to the caller via the JWT subject and role; no filters or pagination.
- Each entry exposes method_type, masked last 4 digits (cards only), and the default flag. The raw card number and gateway token are never returned.

**Use Cases:**
- Render the saved-cards picker before a wallet top-up.
- Show which method is currently the default.

403.description: Caller is not a wallet owner (admin roles have no payment methods)

post.description:
Tokenize and save a new payment method for the authenticated rider or captain.

**Features:**
- For a card, the raw PAN is read only to derive the last 4 digits and a gateway token; only the masked last 4 and the token are stored, and the token is never returned.
- When set_as_default is true, the new method is promoted to default and the returned row reflects is_default = true.

**Behavior:**
1. If method_type is "card", require card_number, derive last 4, and tokenize via the gateway.
2. Persist the method scoped to the caller.
3. Optionally set it as the default.

**Restrictions:**
- method_type "card" requires card_number of at least 4 characters.
- Caller must be a rider or captain; admin roles cannot save personal methods.

400.description: Missing card_number or card_number too short for a card method

403.description: Caller is not a wallet owner (admin roles cannot save payment methods)

delete.description:
Permanently remove one of the caller's saved payment methods.

**Behavior:**
- Deletes the method row matching the id and the caller's owner identity.
- Has no effect on past transactions; the immutable ledger is untouched.

**Restrictions:**
- The method id must belong to the caller; a non-matching id returns 404 and nothing is deleted.
- Caller must be a rider or captain.
- Returns 204 No Content on success; deletion is irreversible.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the saved payment method to delete

get.description:
Return the online captains currently inside the rider's visible map rectangle, as anonymous car markers for the idle (not-yet-ordered) pickup map.

**This is an ambience feed, not dispatch data.** It answers "are there cars around me right now", nothing else. It is not a reservation, not an availability promise, and gives no way to reach, identify, or follow any captain. Fare and ETA on the quote screen are what set expectations; captains on an active trip are deliberately EXCLUDED: a rider already knows their own captain's real id and exact position from the trip endpoint, so including occupied cars would let them match that position to a marker and follow one named worker all day through this 'anonymous' feed.

**Features:**
- `bbox=minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat` (WGS84) is the visible rectangle: refetch on map pan/zoom by whatever is on screen. Same bbox contract as `GET /api/places/nearby`.
- Only captains flagged online whose last GPS ping is within 5 minutes (the same staleness window the sweep uses to force a silent captain offline) -- so a captain whose phone died is never painted as a live car.
- Capped at 20 cars, ordered nearest to the viewport centre first. An empty `cars` array is a normal answer (no captain on shift there), not an error.

**Privacy -- each car carries ONLY:**
- `id`: an opaque per-day token. Stable for one Asia/Baghdad calendar day so the client can animate the same car between polls; a different token for the same captain tomorrow, so the feed cannot be used to profile anyone day over day. It is NOT the captain id and cannot be resolved to one.
- `latitude` / `longitude`, rounded to 4 decimals (~11 m) -- deliberately coarser than the captain's real fix.
- `heading_deg` (nullable), so the marker points the way the car is driving.
- Nothing else: no name, phone, plate, car star, rating, or trip state.

**Use Cases:**
- The idle pickup map, polled about every 6 s while that screen is foregrounded, animating each marker to its new fix between polls.
- Do NOT use it to track the captain assigned to a trip: that is `GET /api/rider/trips/{id}/captain-location` plus the `rt:trip:{id}` WebSocket, which carry the real, un-rounded position the rider is entitled to.

**Restrictions:**
- Requires any valid bearer token (rider, captain, or admin -- the feed reveals nothing role-specific).
- `bbox` is required; coordinates are clamped into valid WGS84 range, and a rectangle that is still degenerate after clamping (min not strictly < max on an axis) is a structured `400` `{ error, expected_order }` rather than a silent empty `200`. Wrong arity or a non-numeric coordinate is a plain `400` `{ error }`.

**Features:**
- Sets `rider_id` from the JWT and starts the trip in 'pending' status.
- Publishes a `beep.scheduled_trip.created` realtime event on the rider channel.
- Promotion to a live trip happens later via the 60-second scheduler tick, not on this call.
- `star` books a car class (1, 2, or 3; omitted = 1). It is priced from the same per-star per-km rates as an immediate `POST /api/trips` request, and is carried onto the promoted trip's `requested_star` so dispatch looks for the class that was paid for.

**Behavior:**
1. Validate `scheduled_for` is at least 30 minutes and at most 7 days from now.
2. Validate `trip_type` is exactly 'regular' (Abriyah scheduling is not supported in v1).

**Restrictions:**
- `scheduled_for` is RFC3339/ISO 8601 UTC; under 30 minutes ahead returns 400, over 7 days ahead returns 400.
- `trip_type` must be 'regular'; any other value returns 400.
- `star` must be 1, 2, or 3; any other value returns 400 (it is rejected, not clamped). The class cannot be changed afterwards -- cancel and rebook.
- The fare is not computed or quoted here; it is struck at promotion from the rates in force at that moment. Use `GET /api/trips/estimate` with the same `star` for a pre-booking figure.
- Coordinates are WGS84 lat/lng.
